correctness.rationale: For height at most two, eliminate each predecessor maximum to obtain an explicit convex image. Every differentiable chamber Jacobian is an orthogonal direct sum of weighted stars. A star with total squared weight U has squared singular values solving z²-(2+U)z+1, so both it and its inverse have sharp norm sqrt((2+U+sqrt(U²+4U))/2). The maximal assigned star weight cannot exceed the maximum weighted incident sum W; a strict interior point with a globally largest selected minimal coordinate realizes W. Convex-domain piecewise-affine chord subdivision proves global upper bounds and singular-vector interior chords attain both. A 4,754-configuration independent numerical checker independently reconstructs 31,079 matrices and tests 9,508 point pairs. Finite tests are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The optimal ordinary Euclidean conditioning of an entire continuous polytope transfer family is a natural geometric invariant absent from the foundational existence/Ehrhart theory. The theorem completely classifies it using a single weighted maximal star, independent of all other bipartite incidences, and gives simultaneous optimal perturbation constants for the map and inverse with interior extremizers. It identifies a genuine incidence-to-metric rigidity and quantitatively bounds deformation of canonical geometric bijections; it is not a numeric experiment or arbitrary parameter slice.
